newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier as stocks end off lows.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends easier as stocks end off lows.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract closed lower on Tuesday as a late recovery in the Tokyo stock market triggered light long-liquidation.

The Nikkei stock average of leading 225 shares closed 25.66 points or 0.14 percent lower at 18,093.13. The index earlier fell more than 500 points but managed to claw back most of its losses in the afternoon.
"The contract is likely to remain underpinned at or above 99.28-99.29 unless the government introduces fiscal measures to support the stock market," said another city bank dealer.

Meanwhile, the key contract's topside is likely to be capped below its life-time high of 99.36, traders said. It may rise above that level only if the central bank provides increased liquidity to the money market to help support share prices, they said.
As was expected, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) conducted a neutral money market operation this morning.
